name: Really Sans
classification_notes: Two-optical-size sans serif family with distinct Large and Small variants. The Large has a higher x-height, tighter spacing and a more geometric construction for display use; the Small opens up spacing and lowers the x-height for running text legibility. Vertically cut open terminations and round diacritical dots align it with the geometric grotesque tradition. Weight range spans Hairline through Ultra in the Large optical size.
summary: A 28-style sans with two genuine optical sizes — Large for display, Small for text — built around open terminations, a Hairline-to-Ultra weight range and broad multilingual coverage.
description: Really Sans addresses a straightforward design problem: sans serifs are called on at both display and text sizes, so the family ships two distinct optical variants rather than asking one design to do everything. The Large variant takes a geometric, tightly spaced approach suited to headlines; the Small pulls back the x-height and loosens spacing for legibility in body copy. Vertically cut terminations, round dots on the i and j, stylistic alternates and a full OpenType feature set — including multiple figure styles, dynamic fractions and directional arrows — give the family real depth across 200+ languages.
foundry_blurb: Lettermatic built Really Sans around a simple observation: designers reach for sans serifs at both large and small sizes, so the typeface should actually work at both. Web and desktop licences come bundled together with no extra fees or additional checkboxes.

name: Bezzia
classification_notes: Contemporary slab serif with two distinct terminal types – sharp beak and rounded hook – giving it tonal range within a single family. Progressive serif reduction at heavier weights protects negative space. Notable for a double-storey g with a continuous bowl-tail, squarish curves and varied serif shapes that read as organic rather than mechanical. Occupies the territory between editorial text and display use.
summary: A contemporary slab serif in eight weights with matching italics, drawn from the entomology collections at the California Academy of Sciences and distinguished by mixed terminal styles, a distinctive double-storey g and a thorough OpenType feature set.
description: Bezzia takes its character from insect specimens rather than historical revivals, mixing sharp beak and rounded hook terminals across its letterforms. The design reduces serifs progressively in heavier weights to preserve negative space, and the double-storey g uses a continuous bowl-tail construction that sets it apart from genre conventions. Sixteen styles across eight weights give it range from detailed editorial text to headline use, backed by 200+ language support and features including oldstyle figures, dynamic fractions, f-ligatures in italic and circled figures.
foundry_blurb: Lettermatic presents Bezzia as a typeface that brings academic gravity and natural character to design work, its forms drawn from entomology display cases at the California Academy of Sciences. They describe it as carrying timeless style alongside contemporary letterform thinking – a natural selection, as they put it, for any project that needs both intelligence and warmth.

name: Parclo Sans
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif with open letter terminals designed to let negative space breathe for improved small-size legibility. Capitals R, B and P carry a subtle bow that adds visual energy in all-caps text. Three widths (Standard, Narrow, Condensed) with nine weights and matching italics across all, plus a companion serif family. Designed with mobile app interfaces in mind but scaled for roadside signage.
summary: A 54-style humanist sans-serif spanning three widths and nine weights, designed for legibility across mobile interfaces and large-scale signage alike.
description: Parclo Sans is a humanist sans-serif built for range, from fine print to roadside display, with open letter terminals that let negative space work in its favour at small sizes and at distance. Capitals R, B and P carry a subtle bow that adds visual energy to all-caps settings without tipping into novelty. It ships with matching italics across all three widths and was designed in tandem with Parclo Serif, sharing underlying design qualities across the two families.
foundry_blurb: Lettermatic positions Parclo Sans as a workhorse built for the full range of reading conditions, citing mobile app interfaces as the original design brief while noting its legibility holds from fine print to roadside signage. The foundry includes both web and desktop licences in every standard purchase, with no additional fees.

name: Parclo Serif
classification_notes: A contemporary upright serif with a wide weight range (Thin through Ultra) and a true italic where every lowercase letter is substantially redrawn rather than slanted from the roman. Hook-shaped terminals in the lowercase and numerals act as a quiet design signature. The combination of extreme weight range and high-craft italics places it in a contemporary tradition rather than a historical revival.
summary: Nine weights from Thin to Ultra, each paired with a genuinely redrawn italic, and hook-shaped terminals in the lowercase and figures that give it a distinct personality without tipping into the decorative.
description: Parclo Serif runs from Thin to Ultra across nine weights, each with a true italic where the lowercase letterforms are substantially redrawn from scratch rather than slanted from the roman. Hook terminals in the lowercase and numerals carry a consistent visual signature across the full weight range. It ships alongside Parclo Sans, with 200+ language coverage and OpenType support spanning old-style figures, tabular figures, fractions, circled figures and directional arrows.
foundry_blurb: Lettermatic bill Parclo Serif as a face with sleek details and plenty of character that performs from hairline to ultra. The italic is built as a true companion: every lowercase letter is redesigned from scratch rather than derived from the roman. Web and desktop licences are bundled at no extra cost, in line with the foundry's position that great type should be accessible regardless of studio size.
